work.title: Readela 0.3.0: two corrections to the approved popup — the bookmark total apart from the shortcuts, and no broken word in a choice when Help is open
work.ownerAuthorization: Owner instruction of 2026-10-13, after the owner installed the build of b190ac4 in Chrome and found the popup and what it does to work. It authorizes two corrections with their focused verification, commits and plain push: the total of bookmarks shown apart from the shortcuts, with the shortcuts as a small part of their own (a heading with the way to the browser's settings beside it, the assigned keys in two columns, a short state where none is assigned, nothing where the browser tells nothing); and a layout in which opening Help, which makes the popup scroll and so narrower by a scrollbar, breaks no ordinary word in a choice. It asks that the real toolbar popup of Chrome be checked and that the empty strip corrected in b190ac4 not come back. It does not authorize a change of the layout's design, the palettes, the reading or bookmark behaviour, the commands or their keys, permissions, supported sites or the version number; a new feature; merging, a tag, a release, a store submission or a change to Personal OS.

parentPreflight.statement: The parent covers the popup's markup, style and wording, its tests, documents, evidence and builds, and this work stays inside that: the same three files of the popup and the tests. None of its invalidators fired: no file that runs in a conversation, no manifest and no stored form changes; the popup needs no new state, result, permission or setting; no check needs the owner's profile or a signed-in site; Capabilities, Exceptions and the baseline are as recorded; HEAD descends from its baseCommit; the Protocol is at the same revision.

inScope: This record, committed first on the existing branch from baseCommit.

src/ui/popup.html, src/ui/popup.css and src/ui/popup.js: under the bookmark's buttons, the message as it is with the total beside it as secondary information; the shortcuts as a part of their own, with its name, the control that opens the browser's settings beside the name, the assigned keys as pairs of action and key in two aligned columns, the words Not set where none is assigned, and nothing where the browser reports nothing.

The same stylesheet: choices that never break inside a word; in the room a scrollbar leaves, the rows keep their shape with a little less air; where the text is much enlarged or the room very narrow, four choices stand two by two instead of breaking or shrinking.
Unit and end-to-end tests for what changes, among them the popup as Chrome itself opens it, with Help closed and open; pictures and measurements before and after.
Dated evidence made necessary by the above, local Chrome and Firefox builds for the owner's review, and an accurate description of pull request 9.
outOfScope: The order and names of the rows, the palettes, the header, Help's text, the footer, the bookmark's buttons and its messages.
The commands, their names in the manifest, how keys are assigned, permissions.
Everything that runs in a conversation; how bookmarks are saved, found and stored; the fonts; supported sites; the version number.
A wider popup, unless measurements show that nothing smaller keeps a word whole.
A repeat of the hour-long memory comparison.
Merging pull request 9, marking it ready, a tag, a release, a store submission, any write to Personal OS.
